'''Miroslav Fiedler''' (7 April 1926 – 20 November 2015) was a Czech [[mathematician]] known for his contributions to [[linear algebra]], [[graph theory]] and [[algebraic graph theory]].

His article, "Algebraic Connectivity of Graphs", published in the ''Czechoslovak Math Journal'' in 1973, established the use of the [[eigenvalue]]s of the [[Laplacian matrix]] of a graph to create tools for measuring [[algebraic connectivity]] in [[algebraic graph theory]].<ref>Algebraic connectivity of graphs. ''Czechoslovak Math. J.'' '''23'''(98):298 - 305 (1973).</ref> Fiedler is honored by the ''[[algebraic connectivity|Fiedler eigenvalue]]'' (the second smallest eigenvalue of the [[graph Laplacian]]), with its associated ''[[algebraic connectivity|Fiedler eigenvector]]'', as the names for the quantities that characterize algebraic connectivity. Since Fiedler's original contribution, this structure has become essential to large areas of research in [[network theory]], [[Flocking (behavior)|flocking]], [[distributed control]], [[Cluster analysis|clustering]], [[multi-robot applications]] and [[image segmentation]].<ref>[http://www.ustavinformatiky.cz/docs/parte_Fiedler.pdf prof. RNDr. Miroslav Fiedler, DrSc.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151207224500/http://www.ustavinformatiky.cz/docs/parte_Fiedler.pdf |date=2015-12-07 }} {{in lang|cs}}</ref>
